The second pre-release of v5: a guide to moving from v4, a notice when a newer SST is out, faster rebuilds in `sst dev`, and the fixes in 4.21.0 and 4.21.1. It's on npm under the `next-experimental` tag, so an install without a version still gets 4.x. Built on sst-community [v4.21.1](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/releases/tag/v4.21.1) with the fixes on `main` since, and on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

It's a build to try v5 with, on a stage of its own. The v5 components can still change in any way before 5.0.0.

### ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **The functions v5 components create refuse an output for `dev`, `logging`, `url`, `python` and `concurrency`**, as `sst.aws.v5.Function` already did. A queue's subscriber is one. These decide which resources are created, so they have to be plain values. The error names the arg.

### New

- **A guide to moving from v4**, [Migrate From v4](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/blob/v5.0.0-alpha.2/www/src/content/docs/docs/migrate-from-v4.mdx). It covers what to check in your config before you install, how to switch a component, what every v5 component does differently, what a switch can replace, a line for each component, and how to go back.
- **The CLI says when a newer SST is out.** Once a day, in the background, the commands that run your app, like `sst deploy`, `sst diff` and `sst dev`, ask GitHub for the newest release in the CLI's major version, the one `sst upgrade` installs. When there is one, the next run shows ``SST 5.0.0-alpha.3 is available. Run `sst upgrade` to update.`` under the header. Nothing is looked for in CI, or with `SST_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1`.
- **`sst dev` rebuilds the functions a change affects together**, 4 Node.js functions at a time unless `SST_BUILD_CONCURRENCY_FUNCTION` says otherwise, and files saved at once, by a formatter or a `git checkout`, start one rebuild instead of one each. With 16 functions that import a shared module, a change to it took 866ms of builds and takes 329ms.
- **A function can leave the AWS SDK out of its bundle in `sst dev`**, which took one function's build from 53ms to 10ms. The [`nodejs.esbuild`](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/blob/v5.0.0-alpha.2/platform/src/components/aws/function.ts) docs show how. It's then loaded from your `node_modules`, and a deploy still bundles it.

### Fixes

- **A `version` rule in `sst.config.ts` accepts a pre-release when it accepts its release.** `">= 4"` and `"5.x"` accept this one, and `"4.x"` doesn't. `5.0.0-alpha.1` only met a rule that named a pre-release.
- **A function given a `role` no longer looks the role up on every run.** Each lookup was an IAM call per function, so an app with 440 functions sharing one role spent 367s of a no-op `sst dev` on them, and now spends 29s. A v5 `Function` uses a role ARN as it is, and still looks up a role given by name. ([#116](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/116))
- **A `Mysql` without a `version` can be created again.** It defaults to `"8.0"`, and RDS uses its current minor version of MySQL 8.0. The old default, `8.0.40`, is no longer offered. A database you've deployed keeps its version.
- **`sst diff` no longer shows a v5 component's function as deleted** when its args hold a value that's only known on deploy, like the ARN of a layer being replaced.
- **A function's changed build options apply in `sst dev` without a restart.** It kept building with the ones it started with.
- **A killed `sst tunnel` or `sst dev` no longer leaves the tunnel running.** Run `sudo sst tunnel install` again after you update, outside a project folder. ([#101](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/101), [anomalyco/sst#6297](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6297))
- **A Go function no longer changes when only the git commit changes**, so a deploy no longer uploads every Go function after each commit. The first deploy after you update uploads each one once. ([#109](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/109), [anomalyco/sst#6976](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6976))
- **The `Run` resource no longer hangs on a long line of output.** ([#110](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/110), [anomalyco/sst#7006](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/7006))

### Docs

- How a `Router` URL route's timeouts behave ([#112](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/112)), and `successor` on PlanetScale's `PostgresBranchRole` ([#111](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/111)).

### Known issues

- **Not ported yet:** the sites (`Nextjs`, `Astro`, `StaticSite` and the rest), `Vpc`, `Router`, `Cdn`, `MicroVm`, the Cloudflare and Vercel components, and others. They work as 4.x components. The [plan](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/blob/v5.0.0-alpha.2/docs/plans/v5-components.md#status) lists them.
- **`sst diff` can still show a 4.x component's function as deleted** that the deploy then updates, as above.
- **Not tried in AWS yet:** `sst dev` with a v5 `Service` or `Task`, `get` and `existing` with real resources, a custom `provider`, and switching a v5 component back to 4.x.
- **The v5 docs aren't published.** The component pages and guides are in the repo, under [`www/src/content/docs/docs`](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/tree/v5.0.0-alpha.2/www/src/content/docs/docs).

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@5.0.0-alpha.2
```

To try it in an existing project:

1. Use a stage of its own. A `version` rule in `sst.config.ts` has to accept 5.x: `">= 4"` does, and an app without one runs with any version.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@5.0.0-alpha.2"` and reinstall.
3. To go back, switch any v5 components back to their 4.x names and check `sst diff`, then set it to `4.21.1`.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. This replaces a global 4.x CLI:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | VERSION=5.0.0-alpha.2 bash
```
